brief.headline: The missing exchange board has been published and it confirmed the read this page held rather than guessed - and the metal has come back to a four-week high with its curve paying a token for prompt metal for the second time in five sessions, just as a new round of North American metals tariffs takes effect today.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The exchange published both missing sessions overnight. Friday settled at $3,292.50 a tonne and Monday at $3,310.00, up 0.53% on the day and the highest settlement since 11-August. Almost none of that is the dollar: the exchange's own euro-dollar fixing barely moved and the dollar index eased 0.22%, so the move is priced in the metal. It was a broad session rather than an aluminium story - zinc rose 1.71% and copper 1.18%, while nickel was the only base metal lower.

WHY THE CURVE MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE TODAY. Cash settled two dollars above the three-month for the second time in five sessions, so the market is once again paying something - barely - to hold metal now rather than later. Set against warehouse stock at a thirty-six-year low that is the direction you would expect, but the amount is two-hundredths of one percent and the front of the curve has been within two dollars of flat for six straight sessions. Treat it as the tension easing slightly, not as a shortage arriving.

THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT KEEPS WEAKENING AT THE MARGIN. Warehouse stock did not move at all on Monday, a published change of exactly zero, and it has fallen just 2,400 tonnes across the last three weeks - under 0.1% of the total per session. The level is still extreme and still the single strongest support for the price; the flow has stopped supporting it. Shanghai inventories, by contrast, fell 3% on the week, so the two visible series are telling different stories.

WHAT TO WATCH, IN ORDER. First, today's North American tariff escalation: Canada's counter-tariffs take effect on 8-September, lifting duties on US steel and aluminium from 25% to 50% across more than 300 metals products and $27.6 billion of imports, which taxes flows in both directions across the largest primary-aluminium trade corridor in the world. Second, two central-bank decisions inside a week - the European Central Bank on Thursday with a quarter-point rise fully priced, and the US Federal Reserve on 16-September after employment printed roughly three times consensus. Third, the Asian quarterly premium, where producers have opened around a fifth below the record and buyers are pushing lower still.

lme.commentary: THE 07-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL PUT CASH AT $3,310.00, UP $17.50 OR 0.53% ON FRIDAY'S $3,292.50 AND THE HIGHEST CASH SETTLEMENT SINCE 11-AUGUST. Three-month rose $15.00 to $3,308.00, so cash settled $2.00 ABOVE the forward and THE CURVE FLIPPED BACK INTO BACKWARDATION for the second time in five sessions. Warehouse stock was UNCHANGED at 244,525 tonnes - a published change of exactly zero. THE PUBLICATION GAP THAT HELD THIS PAGE FOR TWO RUNS IS CLOSED. Both the 04-September and the 07-September LME officials are now public, the board sits on ONE UNIFORM 07-SEPTEMBER SESSION, and the held figures have been replaced by real prints rather than quietly restated. THE HOLD WAS VINDICATED: the 04-September aluminium official settled at $3,292.50, against the independent CFD reference of $3,292.65 that this page carried in commentary but deliberately refused to write into the official board. Fifteen cents apart. Nothing was ever invented to cover the gap and nothing needed to be unwound. THREE THINGS ARE WORTH SEPARATING IN THIS SESSION. FIRST, THE MOVE IS METAL RATHER THAN CURRENCY, and unusually cleanly so: the LME EUR/USD fixing moved 0.02% and the dollar index eased 0.22%, which leaves essentially the entire 0.53% priced in the metal itself. SECOND, IT IS A BOARD-WIDE BID RATHER THAN AN ALUMINIUM SQUEEZE. Zinc cash rose 1.71% to $4,157.00 with its backwardation widening to $182.00 despite 925 tonnes going into warehouse; copper cash rose 1.18% with its backwardation widening to $92.00 despite a 2,300-tonne build; lead added 0.21%; nickel was the only metal lower at -0.54%. Aluminium was mid-pack. A reader looking for a single-metal tightness signal on this board should be looking at zinc, not aluminium. THIRD, THE INVENTORY FLOW HAS STOPPED CONFIRMING THE INVENTORY LEVEL. Stock is unchanged on the session and down only 2,400 tonnes across the fifteen sessions on this page, which is under 0.1% of the total per session. The thirty-six-year low is real and it is repeatedly cited in public commentary as a core support; the draw that produced it has flattened. LEVEL AND FLOW ARE DIFFERENT ARGUMENTS AND ONLY THE LEVEL REMAINS BULLISH. THE HONEST NET OF THE THREE IS A METAL AT THE TOP OF A FOUR-WEEK RANGE, SUPPORTED BY A GENUINE BUT STATIC INVENTORY POSITION AND A CURVE THAT PAYS CENTS RATHER THAN DOLLARS FOR PROMPT UNITS, heading into a week of central-bank tightening risk and a live escalation in North American metals tariffs.

regional.basis: S&P GLOBAL PLATTS SETTLED THE Q3-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM AT A RECORD $395/t CIF JAPAN, ASSESSED 06-JULY-2026, UP 12.4% ON Q2-2026's $351.50/t. THIS IS A CONTRACTED QUARTERLY BENCHMARK, NOT A DAILY PRICE, AND IT IS CARRIED AT ITS SETTLEMENT VALUE UNTIL Q4 RESOLVES - it is not stale, it is simply the number that governs the quarter. THE FORWARD PICTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE HEADLINE AND IT IS PUBLIC: Reuters reported on 02-September, citing four sources involved in the talks, that producers including Rio Tinto and South32 have offered $310-$325/t for October-December, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian volumes.

SPOT CIF JAPAN IS A PERIODIC ASSESSMENT CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK OF $370/t AND NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC ASSESSMENT WAS RETRIEVABLE THIS MORNING. THE STALENESS IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN DISGUISED, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LIMITATION ON THIS PANEL FOR A PHYSICAL READER. WHAT THE SPOT-VERSUS-CONTRACT GAP IMPLIES IS WORTH STATING: a $370 spot against a $395 contracted quarterly settlement means the quarter was contracted above where the market has since been clearing, which is exactly the condition that produces a large downward reset at the next negotiation - and the published Q4 producer offers of $310-325 are consistent with that arithmetic rather than a surprise against it.

EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID IS CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED ASSESSMENT OF $485/t AND NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK WAS RETRIEVABLE. THE EUROPEAN LEG HAS BECOME AN EXPLICIT INPUT INTO THE ASIAN BENCHMARK AND THAT IS THE REASON TO WATCH IT: the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese offers cites softer premiums in Europe alongside a positive progress report on Middle East production. EUROPE IS ALSO WHERE THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE LANDS - the EU import ban on Russian primary aluminium takes effect 31-December-2026, and this is the premium that must absorb it. A soft duty-unpaid premium three months ahead of a ban on a major supply source is a genuine puzzle worth holding in mind.

ROTTERDAM BILLET DUTY-PAID IS CARRIED AT $1,212.50/t, ITS LAST PUBLISHED ASSESSMENT, WITH NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK RETRIEVABLE. BILLET PREMIUM IS THE CLEANEST AVAILABLE READ ON EUROPEAN EXTRUSION DEMAND BECAUSE IT IS PAID BY FABRICATORS RATHER THAN TRADERS, AND IT SITS WELL ABOVE ITS PRIOR-PERIOD AVERAGE OF $1,144. THE DEMAND BACKDROP BEHIND IT DETERIORATED THIS WEEK: Volkswagen's management board confirmed on 05-September that it will close four German plants by 2034 - Emden and Zwickau in 2031, Hanover in 2032, Neckarsulm in 2034 - and guided full-year 2026 group sales down to approximately 8.5 million units. That is a dated, disclosed, structural reduction in European automotive aluminium demand, and while the plant closures are years out the volume guidance is now.

THE US MIDWEST TRANSACTION PRICE IS CARRIED AT $2,094/t, ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK, DOWN SHARPLY FROM THE $2,380 PRIOR AND FROM A PRIOR-PERIOD AVERAGE OF $2,561.90. THIS ROW IS TARIFF-INFLATED AND THAT IS THE ONLY WAY TO READ IT HONESTLY: with Section 232 at 50% on articles, the statutory tariff leg alone on a $3,303.00 cash price is approximately $1,651.50, which is roughly 79% of the entire quoted premium. THE REMAINING FIFTH IS THE ACTUAL PHYSICAL MARKET. A reader who treats this number as a demand signal will misread it completely; it is primarily a tax, and it mechanically rises whenever the metal price rises even if physical conditions are unchanged.

THE DUTY-PAID US MIDWEST ROW MATCHES THE TRANSACTION ROW AT $2,094/t BY CONSTRUCTION AND IS CARRIED AT THE SAME LAST PUBLISHED MARK. THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS REFRESHED EVERY RUN EVEN WHEN THE ASSESSMENT IS NOT, BECAUSE THE TARIFF LEG IS A CALCULATION ON THE VERIFIED RATE AND THE CURRENT CASH PRICE RATHER THAN AN ASSESSMENT: 50% of $3,303.00 is $1,651.50. THE RATE ITSELF IS RE-VERIFIED EACH RUN AND REMAINS 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES, WITH ANNEX I-C CARVE-OUTS AT 15% FOR JAPAN, KOREA, THE UNITED KINGDOM, SWITZERLAND, TAIWAN AND THE EUROPEAN UNION. A reported US-Canada reduction to 25% has been discussed publicly but is NOT law and is not reflected here.

drivers.text: Q4-2026 producer offers are public and 18-22% below the Q3 record, and no newer dated report printed this run — Reuters reported on 02-September-2026, citing four sources involved in the quarterly talks, that top global producers including Rio Tinto and South32 offered Japanese buyers $310-$325 per tonne for October-December shipments, down 18% to 22% on the Q3 settlement of $395. Japanese buyers are targeting below $300. The stated rationale is a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer premiums in Europe, with Iran-related shipment disruption and strong Japanese semiconductor-related demand cited as offsetting support. Talks began the week of 24-August and run through later this month. THE PENDING RANGE ON THIS PAGE IS HELD AT $290-325 AND HAS NOT BEEN NARROWED, because narrowing it without a newer dated source would be judgement presented as data.
drivers.source: Reuters via MINING.COM, 02-Sep-2026 - aluminium producers offer Japanese buyers lower Q4 premiums

drivers.text: The spot-versus-contract gap already implies the reset - the Q4 offers are arithmetic, not a surprise — Spot CIF Japan was last publicly assessed at $370 per tonne against a contracted Q3 settlement of $395, so the quarter was contracted $25 ABOVE where the market has since been clearing. That is precisely the condition that produces a downward reset at the next negotiation, and the published producer offers of $310-325 are consistent with that arithmetic rather than a shock against it. A READER WHO ONLY WATCHES THE HEADLINE QUARTERLY NUMBER WILL SEE A RECORD PREMIUM; the spot assessment and the offer range together show a market that has already moved on.
drivers.source: Platts/periodic public assessments as carried on the premium panel of this page; Reuters via MINING.COM 02-Sep-2026 for the offer range

drivers.text: The North American leg re-priced today and the corridor is now taxed in both directions — Canada's counter-tariffs take effect on 08-September-2026 and explicitly include aluminium: counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium rise from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars. US Section 232 is unchanged and verified at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives. THE TARIFF LEG OF THE US DELIVERED PREMIUM IS DECOMPOSED ON THIS PAGE EVERY RUN AS THE VERIFIED RATE APPLIED TO THE CURRENT CASH SETTLEMENT, and no freight, financing or tightness split is fabricated beneath it. The new Canadian leg supports delivered premiums on both sides of the border while suppressing the volume that crosses.
drivers.source: Department of Finance Canada - list of US products subject to counter-tariffs effective 8-September-2026

drivers.text: The European leg is soft ahead of the largest scheduled supply event on the page, and that is a genuine puzzle — European duty-unpaid was last assessed at $485 per tonne, below its own trailing average, and the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese producer offers explicitly cites SOFTER premiums in Europe. The EU import ban on Russian primary aluminium takes effect on 31-December-2026 and this is the premium that must absorb it. A SOFT DUTY-UNPAID PREMIUM LESS THAN FOUR MONTHS AHEAD OF A BAN ON A MAJOR SUPPLY SOURCE ADMITS TWO READINGS - a market that has already sourced replacement units, or a market that has not yet priced the event - and the assessment cadence is too slow to distinguish them. Both are live and neither should be asserted.
drivers.source: European premium assessments as carried on the premium panel of this page; Reuters via MINING.COM 02-Sep-2026 for the European-softness rationale

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: Carried at its last dated public assessment; NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK PRINTED INTO THE 08-SEPTEMBER COMPILE WINDOW and nothing has been interpolated or estimated. THE ASSESSMENT DATE IS SHOWN ON THE ROW SO THE STALENESS IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN IMPLIED. THE FORWARD VIEW DID MOVE THIS RUN EVEN THOUGH THE MARKS DID NOT, and it is public: SMM expects the SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE, describing a market entering September in surplus with high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup keeping absolute prices under pressure. THE STRUCTURAL READ IS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED: the refinery side of the chain remains in surplus while the smelter side is disrupted, and Alunorte has ramped back to full capacity from its August 50% cut on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier. That temporary agreement remains the single largest identifiable upside risk to alumina and therefore the largest downside risk to smelter margin. FOR A COST READER THE IMPORTANT NUANCE THIS MONTH IS THAT THE STACK IS MOVING TWO WAYS AT ONCE - SMM expects prebaked anode and aluminium fluoride prices to RISE over the same period, so a falling alumina headline does not by itself imply a falling total cash cost.

alumina.notes: ALUMINA REMAINS THE ONE PART OF THE VALUE CHAIN IN GENUINE SURPLUS AND THAT IS WHY SMELTER MARGINS HAVE BEEN WIDE ALL YEAR. NO NEW PUBLIC ASSESSMENT PRINTED INTO THIS WEEKEND WINDOW, SO EVERY ROW ON THIS PANEL IS CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED MARK WITH THE DATE SHOWN, AND NOTHING IS INTERPOLATED. SMM's market commentary continues to describe the Chinese alumina market as one of STRONG SUPPLY AND WEAK DEMAND that limits rebound room, which is consistent with the refinery-side surplus this page has been reporting. THE SINGLE LARGEST IDENTIFIABLE RISK TO THAT SURPLUS IS ALUNORTE, THE LARGEST REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA. It cut production to 50% of capacity during August in a natural-gas supply dispute and has since ramped back to full capacity following a TEMPORARY TERMINAL ACCESS AGREEMENT with its gas supplier. The word temporary is the whole risk: the restoration is conditional on an expiring arrangement rather than on a resolved dispute, and the same disruption previously drove Norsk Hydro to declare force majeure on aluminium sales. A RENEWED ALUNORTE INTERRUPTION WOULD COMPRESS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT MARGIN DRIVER IN THE INDUSTRY, WHICH MAKES IT THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED RISK ON THIS PAGE. The reason it is under-weighted is that alumina surplus is a quiet, structural, boring fact while the metal-side inventory headline is dramatic - and this week demonstrated that the dramatic fact was the less reliable one.

Contracts are bilateral, confidential, jurisdiction-specific and often decades long, so any chart drawn here would be an invention rather than a measurement. THE ROW IS CARRIED AS A RANGE WITH THE CONSUMPTION RATIO SHOWN BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT CAN HONESTLY BE PUBLISHED. items.label: Aluminium fluoride (AlF3)
items.note: NEW PUBLIC MARK APPENDED THIS RUN - THE FIRST NUMERIC POINT ADDED TO THIS ROW SINCE 16-AUGUST. SMM's fluoride-salt weekly review, published 05-September-2026 and carried by AL Circle, puts mainstream SMM quotations for aluminium fluoride at RMB 11,500-12,000 per tonne, up from the RMB 11,200-11,800 range carried previously. THE POINT APPENDED IS 11,500 BECAUSE THIS ROW'S HIST SERIES IS CONSISTENTLY BUILT ON THE LOW END OF THE SMM MAINSTREAM RANGE - the 16-August point of 11,200 was the low end of 11,200-11,800 - and changing basis mid-series would corrupt the sparkline. THE DRIVERS ARE DISCLOSED AND SPECIFIC. Benchmark downstream enterprises finalised September tender prices during the week and raised them by RMB 300-500 per tonne overall, with the high-grade transaction centre climbing to RMB 12,000-12,500 per tonne. The cost push is upstream fluorspar: 97% fluorite wet powder is at RMB 3,350-3,850 per tonne delivered and holding firm at high levels, because high-pressure mine safety inspections have continued unabated - Inner Mongolia's 'Double Ten Measures' inspections, Zhejiang's small-mine closure policy, and ongoing compliance checks in Jiangxi and Fujian have delayed production resumptions and kept fluorite inventory low. Anhydrous hydrogen fluoride September long-term contracts were raised above RMB 15,000 per tonne. Partly offsetting, aluminium hydroxide was flat week on week at an SMM weighted average of RMB 1,650 per tonne and sulphuric acid eased. SMM'S OWN SUMMARY OF THE MARKET IS 'COST SUPPORT, TIGHT SUPPLY, AND INELASTIC DEMAND', with producers running at low operating loads on narrow margins and prioritising long-term contract delivery. THE READ-ACROSS FOR A SMELTER IS THAT THIS IS A COST INCREASE DRIVEN ENTIRELY BY CHINESE MINE-SAFETY ENFORCEMENT UPSTREAM - it will not respond to aluminium demand and it will not ease until fluorspar supply is released.

THE TREND FLAG IS CUT FROM FLAT TO UP: this series sat at RMB 7,000 from May through late June, moved to 7,500 in August and is now at 8,000, which is a 14.3% increase from the spring plateau and the first genuinely sustained move in the row. THE CAUSE IS THE SAME AS THE ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE ROW AND THAT IS THE POINT WORTH DRAWING OUT: both are fluorine chemistry, both depend on fluorspar, and Chinese mine-safety enforcement is now visibly repricing the entire bath-chemistry basket at once rather than one line at a time. Consumption is small at roughly 10 kg per tonne of metal, so the absolute margin impact is modest, but two correlated bath inputs moving together is a cleaner signal about upstream fluorspar than either one alone.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE ROW IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND THE RISK INTENSIFIED THIS WEEK. Trading Economics reported that the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over the potential return of aluminium supplies from the Persian Gulf. THE PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCES REMAIN VISIBLE ACROSS THREE SEPARATE PRODUCERS - EGA at 315 of 1,262 cells with its refinery at roughly 50%, Qatalum curtailed at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas, and Alba with reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March. THE TENSION WORTH NAMING IS THAT PRODUCERS CITED A POSITIVE MIDDLE EAST PROGRESS REPORT WHEN CUTTING Q4 JAPANESE PREMIUM OFFERS 18-22%: the disruption is real and the market's willingness to pay for it is falling at the same time.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: RE-STATED THIS RUN ON A CURRENT PUBLIC BASIS RATHER THAN CARRIED. Traffic through Bab el Mandeb is down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and the US Maritime Administration advisory 2026-006 covering the Red Sea, Bab el Mandeb, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea and Somali Basin REMAINS IN FORCE THROUGH 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Suez transits remain far below pre-crisis normal and carriers are still routing via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. THE DIRECTION FLAG IS DOWN BECAUSE THE CORRIDOR IS DEGRADED, NOT BECAUSE COSTS ARE FALLING - the two Middle East chokepoints on this page are now both impaired simultaneously, Hormuz by live hostilities and Bab el Mandeb by a blockade with a dated advisory attached, and a producer routing Gulf or Red Sea metal to Europe has no unimpaired option. Sources: https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2026-006-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-gulf-aden-arabian-sea-and-somali-basin-houthi-attacks ; https://gcaptain.com/suez-canal-traffic-stalls-at-60-below-normal-despite-100-days-without-houthi-attacks/

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: STILL NO PUBLIC REPRICE, AND THE ABSENCE IS NOW OLD ENOUGH TO BE A FINDING RATHER THAN A GAP. The last public mark this page can cite is 7.5-10% of hull value from 22-July, against a 1-3% pre-conflict norm. Since that mark, at least four merchant vessels have been reported struck in or near the Strait, including two on Monday night and further attacks reported on 01/02-September. HULL-VALUE PREMIUM IS THE FIRST THING THAT REPRICES AFTER TANKERS ARE PHYSICALLY HIT, so the 22-July figure should be treated as a FLOOR and explicitly not as a current quote. This page will not estimate the current level because war-risk rates are negotiated bilaterally and no public assessment exists. THE COMMERCIAL POINT STANDS WITHOUT THE NUMBER: war-risk cost sits inside every regional premium on this page simultaneously and is completely invisible in the LME flat price, which is one reason a falling LME and firm premiums are not the contradiction they appear to be.

logistics.note: CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK WITH THE STALENESS DISCLOSED; DRY-BULK INDICES DO NOT PUBLISH AT THE WEEKEND AND NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED. THE BDI MATTERS TO THIS INDUSTRY PRINCIPALLY THROUGH BAUXITE AND ALUMINA RATHER THAN THROUGH METAL, because the upstream legs of the chain are the bulk-freight legs: roughly two tonnes of alumina and four to five tonnes of bauxite move for every tonne of metal produced. A freight move is therefore an upstream cost event with a lag, not a metal-price event.

CONTAINER FREIGHT IS THE WRONG INDEX FOR PRIMARY METAL AND IS RETAINED FOR THE DOWNSTREAM LEG: extrusions, rolled coil, finished components and value-added products move in boxes rather than in bulk. IT IS THEREFORE THE FREIGHT LINE THAT BEARS ON THE FABRICATED-PRODUCT PREMIUMS ON THIS PAGE - Rotterdam billets, Southeast Asian billet premiums - rather than on the LME price.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: GENERIC COMMERCIAL NOTE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN - BUT WITH A NEW FORWARD-LOOKING POINT WORTH FLAGGING GENERICALLY. Contracts written across the Gulf disruption commonly carry force-majeure, war-risk cost-pass-through and demurrage clauses that were drafted for a CLOSED strait. A partial, temporary, 30-to-60-day corridor arrangement of the kind announced on 26-August sits awkwardly between 'closed' and 'open' and is exactly the situation in which such clauses become contested rather than automatic. Anyone with live tonnage under those terms should expect the interpretation question to arrive before the logistics question resolves. This is a general market observation about contract structure and carries no company-specific or confidential content.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: BRENT WAS $97.57 AT THIS COMPILE, UP 1.34%, WITH WTI AT $92.31, UP 0.91%. ENERGY IS THE LARGEST SINGLE COST LINE IN A SMELTER AND THE MOST IMPORTANT MACRO ROW ON THIS PAGE FOR A COST READER. The rise is consistent with the Strait of Hormuz situation remaining unresolved rather than with demand strength, which is the uncomfortable combination for this industry: THE SAME DISRUPTION THAT SUPPORTS THE METAL PRICE ALSO RAISES THE COST OF PRODUCING IT AND OF SHIPPING IT. A firm crude tape alongside two central banks tightening inside eight days is mildly stagflationary in character, and that is the macro backdrop the 16-September Federal Reserve decision sits against.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: TTF WAS EUR 73.22/MWh AT THIS COMPILE, UP 1.76%, AND IT HAS FIRMED FROM EUR 71.96 AT THE LAST RUN. EUROPEAN GAS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON EUROPEAN SMELTER RESTART ECONOMICS AND THE REASON ROUGHLY HALF OF EU PRIMARY CAPACITY HAS SAT CURTAILED SINCE 2022. THE LEVEL MATTERS MORE THAN THE DAILY MOVE AND IT IS STILL HIGH ENOUGH TO KEEP MOST RESTART DECISIONS MARGINAL - which is precisely why Slovalco is being restarted with a Slovak government carbon-compensation agreement behind it rather than on merchant power alone, why Alcoa needed energy hedging through 2027 at San Ciprian, and why Portland needed secured power to mid-2035. GAS IS ALSO THE CHANNEL THROUGH WHICH THE GULF DISRUPTION REACHES EUROPEAN COST, since Middle East LNG scarcity and European gas pricing are linked.

row.label: US dollar index
row.note: THE DOLLAR INDEX EASED 0.22% TO 98.956 AND THE LME'S OWN EUR/USD FIXING MOVED JUST 0.02%, FROM 1.16210 TO 1.16230. THIS IS WHY THE ALUMINIUM MOVE IS READ AS METAL RATHER THAN CURRENCY THIS SESSION, AND IT IS AN UNUSUALLY CLEAN READING: with the currency essentially static, effectively the whole 0.53% cash advance is priced in the metal itself rather than borrowed from a weaker dollar. THE FORWARD TENSION IS THAT A HAWKISH FEDERAL RESERVE ON 16-SEPTEMBER WOULD PUSH THIS ROW THE OTHER WAY. A dollar-priced industrial metal carries a mechanical headwind from dollar strength that is independent of anything happening in its own supply and demand, and the market has moved from pricing a cut to pricing the possibility of a hike inside a fortnight.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: THE EURO WAS $1.16223 AT THIS COMPILE, UP 0.07%, AGAINST AN LME FIXING OF 1.16230. THIS ROW MATTERS FOR TWO REASONS. FIRST, IT IS THE CURRENCY ADJUSTMENT ON THE HEADLINE PRICE: aluminium rose 0.53% in dollars and, with the fixing essentially flat, close to the same in euros, so European buyers saw very nearly the full move rather than a currency-muted version of it. SECOND, THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECIDES ON THURSDAY 10-SEPTEMBER WITH A QUARTER-POINT RISE FULLY PRICED after euro-area August inflation rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. A rise that is fully priced moves this row only if the guidance surprises, so the risk here is two-sided rather than directional.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: THE US TEN-YEAR WAS 4.789% AT THIS COMPILE. THE LEVEL IS THE POINT RATHER THAN THE DAILY MOVE, AND IT IS THE SINGLE CLEANEST TRANSMISSION CHANNEL FROM MACRO INTO THIS INDUSTRY'S SUPPLY SIDE. Every curtailed smelter weighing a restart is discounting a long stream of future margin against a cost of capital anchored here, and every entry in the restart pipeline on this page - Slovalco, San Ciprian, Portland, Mt Holly, Al Taweelah - required a power solution and a financing decision first. A HIGHER DISCOUNT RATE IS A GENUINE BRAKE ON THE RESTART PIPELINE EVEN AS THE PIPELINE ITSELF WIDENS, which is the main reason the hawkish repricing of the last week is not straightforwardly bearish for the metal.

headlines.title: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT TODAY, 08-SEPTEMBER-2026, AND THEY EXPLICITLY INCLUDE ALUMINIUM. Canada is applying 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on products drawn from those targeted by the US Section 338 and Section 232 measures, with each product's rate matched to the corresponding US rate. IN STEEL AND ALUMINIUM SPECIFICALLY, EXISTING CANADIAN COUNTER-TARIFFS RISE FROM 25% TO 50% to align with the US rate. The measures cover $27.6 billion of imports from the United States and more than 300 metals products and derivatives, including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and are described by the Canadian government as matching the US Section 338 tariffs dollar for dollar following the US decision to impose 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS IS TAGGED MIXED RATHER THAN BULLISH: it taxes flows in BOTH directions across what is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade corridor in the world. It supports regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border by raising the cost of arbitraging between them, and it simultaneously suppresses the volume that actually crosses. For a physical reader the practical effect is that North American premiums and the underlying exchange price become less connected to each other, not more.

THE LME PUBLICATION GAP IS CLOSED AND THE HELD BOARD WAS VINDICATED BY THE ACTUAL PRINT. Both the 04-September and 07-September officials have now been published. THE 04-SEPTEMBER ALUMINIUM OFFICIAL SETTLED AT $3,292.50 CASH, $3,293.00 THREE-MONTH, 244,525 TONNES. This page had refused for two consecutive runs to write any 04-September figure into the official board, holding it at 03-September and disclosing the hold on every panel, while carrying an independent CFD reference of $3,292.65 in commentary only. THE TWO MEASUREMENTS LANDED FIFTEEN CENTS APART. Nothing was invented, nothing needed unwinding, and the same rule will apply at the next gap. THE SOURCE IS STILL INTERNALLY UNEVEN, IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO LATE AUGUST: the English and cache-busted German overviews both carry 07-September and agree line for line, the per-metal nickel, zinc and lead tables have caught up, but the aluminium and copper per-metal tables still end at 04-September - so those two rows were reconciled arithmetically to the tonne against the published stock changes before use.

ALUMINIUM SETTLED AT $3,310.00 ON 07-SEPTEMBER, UP $17.50 OR 0.53%, THE HIGHEST CASH OFFICIAL SINCE 11-AUGUST, AND THE CURVE FLIPPED BACK INTO A $2.00 BACKWARDATION. Three-month rose $15.00 to $3,308.00. This is the second backwardation print in five sessions after two sessions of $0.50 contango. THE MOVE IS METAL RATHER THAN CURRENCY: the LME EUR/USD fixing moved 0.02% and the dollar index eased 0.22%, leaving essentially the whole advance priced in the metal. IT WAS ALSO A BOARD-WIDE BID RATHER THAN AN ALUMINIUM SQUEEZE - zinc cash rose 1.71%, copper 1.18%, lead 0.21%, and nickel was the only base metal lower at -0.54% - so aluminium was mid-pack. THE CAVEAT THAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING A STRONGER SIGNAL is size: a $2.00 backwardation on a $3,310 metal is two-hundredths of one percent, and the front of the curve has now been within $2.00 of flat for six consecutive sessions.

LME ALUMINIUM STOCK WAS UNCHANGED AT 244,525 TONNES ON 07-SEPTEMBER - A PUBLISHED CHANGE OF EXACTLY ZERO - AFTER DRAWING 1,450 TONNES ON 04-SEPTEMBER. Across the fifteen published sessions from 17-August to 07-September stock has fallen from 246,925 to 244,525 tonnes: a draw of 2,400 tonnes in three weeks, or under 0.1% of the total per session. THE LEVEL AND THE FLOW NOW POINT DIFFERENT WAYS AND THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NUANCE ON THE PAGE. The thirty-six-year low is real and is repeatedly cited in public commentary as a core support for the price; the draw that produced it has flattened to the point of stopping. A market being drained looks different from this. THE CONTRARY EVIDENCE IS REPORTED FOR BALANCE: Shanghai exchange inventories fell 3% week on week on their latest published mark, so the Chinese visible series is still tightening even as the London one goes flat.

ZINC IS THE REAL TIGHTNESS SIGNAL ON THIS BOARD, NOT ALUMINIUM, AND IT IS WORTH FLAGGING BECAUSE IT SHAPES HOW THE ALUMINIUM CURVE SHOULD BE READ. Zinc cash settled at $4,157.00 on 07-September, up $70.00 or 1.71%, with three-month at $3,975.00 - a BACKWARDATION OF $182.00, which WIDENED on the session even as 925 tonnes were delivered into warehouse. Copper's backwardation likewise widened to $92.00 against a 2,300-tonne build. THOSE ARE CURVES PAYING REAL MONEY FOR PROMPT UNITS AGAINST RISING VISIBLE STOCK. Aluminium, with the lowest inventory of the group relative to its own history, is paying $2.00. THE COMPARISON IS THE CLEANEST AVAILABLE EVIDENCE THAT ALUMINIUM'S THIRTY-SIX-YEAR INVENTORY LOW IS NOT CURRENTLY TRANSLATING INTO PHYSICAL SCARCITY AT THE PROMPT DATE - because when a metal genuinely is scarce, this board shows what that looks like.

THE LATEST ESCALATION IN US-IRAN HOSTILITIES HAS RAISED UNCERTAINTY OVER THE POTENTIAL RETURN OF ALUMINIUM SUPPLIES FROM THE PERSIAN GULF, per Trading Economics market commentary carried with the 04-September mark and still current on the page at this compile. This is the pillar of the bull case that has not weakened. Gulf capacity loss is not a forecast - it is observable in published company disclosures: Qatalum is running at roughly 60% of its 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a second Hydro force majeure outstanding, and Aluminium Bahrain has had reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026, representing 19% of its 1,623,000-tonne capacity with no restart announced. LNG supply from the Middle East, which the same commentary describes as essential for aluminium refining, has been scarce on tanker disruption in the Strait.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM EXPORTS ROSE 18.7% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY AND REMAIN THE PRINCIPAL MECHANISM RELIEVING THE WESTERN SHORTAGE. Public commentary attributes the surge to muted domestic demand allowing producers to ship metal out despite Beijing's 45-million-tonne output cap, easing shortages created by the Middle East disruption. THIS IS THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED BEARISH FACT ON THE PAGE for a reader focused on London inventories: the metal relieving the Western market is arriving as semi-finished and alloy product that does not pass through LME warehouses, which is one coherent explanation for why a thirty-six-year exchange inventory low can coexist with a front-month curve that will not pay for prompt metal. THE OUTPUT CEILING IS REAL AND THE EXPORT FLOW IS ALSO REAL; they are not contradictory.

ALUNORTE, THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA, HAS RAMPED BACK TO FULL CAPACITY AFTER ITS AUGUST CUT TO 50%, FOLLOWING A TEMPORARY TERMINAL-ACCESS AGREEMENT WITH ITS GAS SUPPLIER. THE WORD TEMPORARY IS THE WHOLE RISK AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Restored alumina supply relieves the largest purchased input in the smelter cost stack and therefore removes a cost-push support from the aluminium price, which is why this is tagged bearish for the metal even though it is operationally good news. IF THE ARRANGEMENT LAPSES THE EFFECT REVERSES SHARPLY, and this remains the single largest identifiable upside risk to alumina and therefore the largest downside risk to smelter margin on this page.

THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM NEGOTIATION IS OPEN 18-22% BELOW THE Q3 RECORD AND NO NEWER DATED REPORT PRINTED THIS RUN. Reuters reported on 02-September-2026, citing four sources involved in the talks, that top global producers including Rio Tinto and South32 offered Japanese buyers $310-$325 per tonne for October-December shipments, down 18% to 22% on the Q3 settlement of $395, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. The stated rationale is a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer premiums in Europe; concerns over Iran-related shipment disruption and strong Japanese semiconductor-related demand are cited as offsetting support. Talks began the week of 24-August and are expected to run through later this month. THE PENDING RANGE ON THIS PAGE IS THEREFORE HELD AT $290-325 AND HAS NOT BEEN NARROWED, because narrowing it without a newer dated source would be judgement dressed as data.

SMM EXPECTS THE SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE WHILE PREBAKED ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE PRICES BOTH RISE, PUSHING AUXILIARY MATERIAL COSTS UP. Entering September the alumina market is described as maintaining a surplus with high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup, keeping absolute prices under pressure. THE SPLIT IS THE POINT FOR A COST READER AND IT IS WHY THIS IS TAGGED MIXED RATHER THAN BEARISH: the single largest purchased input is easing while the carbon and bath lines are firming, so the direction of total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone. The September prebaked anode settlement is 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t on an acceptance basis.

TWO MAJOR CENTRAL BANKS DECIDE INSIDE EIGHT DAYS AND BOTH ARE TIGHTENING RISKS FOR A DOLLAR-PRICED INDUSTRIAL METAL. The European Central Bank decides on THURSDAY 10-SEPTEMBER with a 25 basis point rise fully priced after euro-area August inflation rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. The US Federal Reserve follows on WEDNESDAY 16-SEPTEMBER, and after August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 - with June and July revised up a combined 55,000, unemployment steady at 4.1% and participation rising to 61.6% - traders are pricing the possibility of a HIKE rather than a cut. THE REGIME THIS PAGE TRACKS HAS FLIPPED: for weeks the open question was whether the Fed would cut; the live question is whether it raises. Higher policy rates raise the discount rate on every curtailed smelter weighing a restart, which is a genuine brake on the restart pipeline even as that pipeline widens.

THE RESTART PIPELINE KEEPS WIDENING ON PUBLIC, DATED SCHEDULES AND EVERY ENTRY SHARES ONE FEATURE. Hydro is restarting 75,000 tonnes at Slovalco in Slovakia, the first tranche of 175,000 tonnes total, after reaching an agreement with the Slovak government on carbon cost compensation, with production guided to begin in Q4-2026. Alcoa's San Ciprian smelter in Spain has restarted and is running close to full capacity after securing energy hedging through 2027, and Alcoa completed the restart of 15,000 tonnes of previously curtailed capacity at Portland in Australia during Q2-2026. Century's Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015. THE COMMON FEATURE IS THAT A POWER SOLUTION CAME FIRST - a government agreement, a secured purchase agreement, or both - which is exactly why this week's hawkish rate repricing is a real constraint on the pipeline rather than a theoretical one.

EGA HAS 315 OF AL TAWEELAH'S 1,262 REDUCTION CELLS BACK ONLINE - ROUGHLY 25% - WITH THE REFINERY AT ABOUT 50% AND PRE-WAR OUTPUT REAFFIRMED FOR Q1-2027. This is the largest single block of disrupted Gulf capacity returning and it is returning on a published schedule rather than a rumour, which is why it is tagged bearish. SEPARATELY, EGA IS REPORTED TO BE IN TALKS WITH THE US GOVERNMENT OVER INCENTIVES TO BUILD A US SMELTER, contingent on securing a competitive long-term power supply and government financial support - the same power-first precondition that governs every other entry in the restart pipeline. A UAE-based producer also announced in September the acquisition of a 110,000 tonne-per-year US secondary aluminium producer in Rosemont, Minnesota.

QATALUM REMAINS CURTAILED AT ROUGHLY 60% OF ITS 648,000-TONNE NAMEPLATE ON REDUCED GAS, WITH A SECOND HYDRO FORCE MAJEURE ON ALUMINIUM SALES OUTSTANDING, AND ALUMINIUM BAHRAIN HAS HAD REDUCTION LINES 1, 2 AND 3 IDLED SINCE MARCH 2026 - 19% OF ITS 1,623,000-TONNE CAPACITY - WITH NO RESTART ANNOUNCED. These are the two cleanest, best-documented capacity losses on the page and neither has a published resolution date. THEY ARE THE REASON THE BULL CASE HAS A FLOOR EVEN AS THE INVENTORY FLOW FLATTENS AND THE RESTART PIPELINE WIDENS: unlike the restart entries, which are scheduled and therefore already discountable, these are open-ended.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT ON 31-DECEMBER-2026 AND THE EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID PREMIUM IS THE PRICE THAT MUST ABSORB IT. This is the largest scheduled structural event on the page. THE PUZZLE WORTH HOLDING IN MIND IS THAT THE PREMIUM IS NOT BEHAVING AS IF IT IS COMING: European duty-unpaid was last assessed at $485/t, below its own trailing average, and the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese producer offers explicitly cites SOFTER premiums in Europe. A soft duty-unpaid premium less than four months ahead of a ban on a major supply source is either a market that has already sourced its replacement units, or a market that has not yet priced the event. Both readings are live and the assessment cadence is too slow to distinguish them.

SOUTH32 HAS ENTERED A BINDING CONDITIONAL AGREEMENT TO SELL ITS ALUMINIUM VALUE CHAIN ASSETS TO ALCOA FOR UP TO $5.6 BILLION, WITH COMPLETION GUIDED TO H1-2027. South32 reported FY26 group underlying EBITDA of $2,462 million, up 28%, and describes the transaction as a pivot to base metals. WITHIN THE DIVISION BEING SOLD THE TWO LEGS MOVED OPPOSITE WAYS AND ROUGHLY CANCELLED: aluminium contributed $435 million of commodity price gains while alumina subtracted $504 million, with alumina EBITDA down $868 million. THIS IS TAGGED MIXED BECAUSE CONSOLIDATION DOES NOT CHANGE TONNES IN THE SHORT RUN - it changes who owns them and how they are financed - but it does concentrate Western primary supply decisions in fewer hands ahead of the European supply reset at year end.

THE DEMAND SIDE REMAINS THE WEAKEST-EVIDENCED PART OF THIS PAGE AND THE LATEST PUBLIC DATAPOINT WAS SOFT. China Passenger Car Association preliminary data put August retail passenger-vehicle sales at 1.626 million units, DOWN 19% year on year though up 11% month on month, with new-energy retail at 1.069 million units, down 4% year on year and up 12% month on month. Automotive is one of the largest end-uses for semi-finished aluminium and a 19% year-on-year decline in the world's largest vehicle market is a material negative. THE HONEST CAVEAT IS THAT ONE MONTH OF RETAIL DATA IN ONE END-USE IS NOT A DEMAND THESIS, and the month-on-month direction was positive; it is reported because the bull case on this page rests almost entirely on supply, and supply-only arguments deserve a demand cross-check.

ENERGY IS FIRM ON BOTH LEGS AND THAT IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE COMBINATION FOR THIS INDUSTRY. Brent was $97.57 per barrel at this compile, up 1.34%, with WTI at $92.31, up 0.91%, and European gas TTF at EUR 73.22 per MWh, up 1.76%. THE SAME DISRUPTION THAT SUPPORTS THE METAL PRICE RAISES THE COST OF PRODUCING AND SHIPPING IT. Electricity is the largest single line in a smelter cash cost at roughly 30-40%, and European gas is the binding constraint on European restart economics - the reason roughly half of EU primary capacity has sat curtailed since 2022 and the reason Slovalco needed a government carbon-compensation agreement and Portland needed secured power to mid-2035 before either could commit. A FIRM CRUDE AND GAS TAPE ALONGSIDE HAWKISH CENTRAL BANKS IS MILDLY STAGFLATIONARY IN CHARACTER, and that is the backdrop the 16-September Federal Reserve decision sits against.

Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

status.name: EGA (Al Taweelah)
status.status: PARTIAL RESTART - 315 OF 1,262 CELLS (~25%); REFINERY ~50%; PRE-WAR OUTPUT REAFFIRMED FOR Q1-2027; SEPARATELY IN TALKS WITH THE US GOVERNMENT OVER INCENTIVES FOR A US SMELTER, CONTINGENT ON COMPETITIVE LONG-TERM POWER
status.impact: Bearish (supply returning on a dated, published schedule)
status.update: RE-CHECKED 07-SEPTEMBER AND CARRIED UNCHANGED - NO NEW DATED COMPANY DISCLOSURE OR PRESS ITEM PRINTED OVER THE WEEKEND. CARRIED AT THE 26-AUGUST-2026 DISCLOSURE AND RE-DATED ONLY, BECAUSE NO NEWER COMPANY STATEMENT PRINTED IN THIS WINDOW. EGA confirmed 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 reduction cells restarted - a quarter of the smelter - after the March Iranian strike on the Khalifa Economic Zone forced an emergency shutdown of all EGA facilities at the site. All three production lines were re-energised between May and August and are being worked simultaneously to speed the recovery, with around 1,000 people involved. Chief Executive Abdulnasser Bin Kalban reiterated the company remains on track to restore FULL PRODUCTION IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 2027. The refinery continues at about 50% capacity and the new recycling plant is increasing output as planned with full output expected by the final quarter of this year; EGA states the pace of further alumina ramp-up will be determined by supply-chain considerations and the optimisation of its alumina sourcing strategy. WHY IT MATTERS TODAY: Al Taweelah is roughly 1.5 Mt/y of nameplate and Reuters puts Middle East capacity at about 9% of the global total, so a restart running to a published schedule is the single largest identified source of returning supply on this panel. It is also the specific fact that Reuters names - a positive progress report on Middle East production - as one of two reasons producers opened the Japanese Q4 premium round 18-22% lower.

Alba initiated a controlled and safe shutdown of reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 in mid-March 2026 to preserve business continuity amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption, idling 19% of its 1,623,000 tpa capacity; asset care and maintenance are being carried out on the idled lines to enable a safe restart 'when conditions permit'. status.name: China operators (aggregate, incl. Chalco and Hongqiao)
status.status: AT OR THROUGH THE 45 Mt POLICY CEILING; OUTPUT STABLE, MARGINS WIDE, EXPORTS ELEVATED AT +18.7% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY
status.impact: Mixed (the supply ceiling is real; the margin says nothing shuts)
status.update: RE-CHECKED 07-SEPTEMBER AND CARRIED UNCHANGED - NO NEW DATED COMPANY DISCLOSURE OR PRESS ITEM PRINTED OVER THE WEEKEND. THE 45 Mt CAPACITY CEILING SET IN 2017 WAS RENEWED UNDER THE 2025-2027 ACTION PLAN AND OPERATING CAPACITY WAS 44.83 Mtpa AT END-AUGUST, so China is running at or through the policy ceiling with no headroom to add. SMM reports domestic production steady week on week with the liquid-aluminium proportion easing marginally. THE NEW DATED POINTS THIS RUN ARE INVENTORY AND PRICE RATHER THAN OUTPUT, AND BOTH ARE BULLISH. Chinese ingot social inventory fell 22,000 t on the week to 815,000 t and is down 37,000 t from the prior Thursday; SHFE exchange inventories have fallen for ELEVEN CONSECUTIVE WEEKS from a six-year high of 528,885 t on 12-June to 391,498 t per Reuters; and the SHFE 2610 contract closed at RMB 24,235/t, up 0.75%, at a new recent high with volume expanding to 91,100 lots. THE OFFSET IS THE EXPORT CHANNEL AND IT IS TURNING BEARISH FOR EX-CHINA BALANCES IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: Chinese exports surged 18.7% in the year to July and have been the principal offset to Middle East supply losses all year, but SMM notes a recovering SHFE/LME ratio is expected to weaken export demand as orders on hand are digested. MARGINS REMAIN THE REASON NOTHING SHUTS: China Hongqiao's H1-2026 gross profit rose 32.3% and Chuangxin's net profit rose 166.1%, both on falling alumina cost. A producer earning that much does not curtail, ceiling or no ceiling.

status.name: US / Canada trade policy (Section 232)
status.status: US 232 UNCHANGED AND VERIFIED AT 50% ON ARTICLES, 25% ON DERIVATIVES. NEW AND LIVE TODAY: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT 08-SEPTEMBER, RAISING CANADIAN COUNTER-TARIFFS ON US STEEL AND ALUMINIUM FROM 25% TO 50% ACROSS $27.6bn OF IMPORTS AND 300+ METALS PRODUCTS
status.impact: Mixed (the corridor is now taxed in BOTH directions - the largest single swing factor in regional delivered premiums)
status.update: RE-CHECKED 07-SEPTEMBER AND CARRIED UNCHANGED - NO NEW DATED COMPANY DISCLOSURE OR PRESS ITEM PRINTED OVER THE WEEKEND. RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE THIS RUN AND UNCHANGED. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085, sets 50% on aluminium articles and Annex I-A derivatives and 25% on Annex I-B derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. A REPORTED US-CANADA REDUCTION TO 25% HAS BEEN DISCUSSED PUBLICLY BUT IS NOT LAW AND IS NOT REFLECTED IN ANY NUMBER ON THIS PAGE. THE ARITHMETIC MOVED TODAY EVEN THOUGH THE POLICY DID NOT, and the mechanism is worth stating because it is counterintuitive: the duty is ad valorem, so at a $3,303.00 cash settlement the pure tariff component of the US delivered premium is 0.50 x $3,303.00 = $1,651.50/t, up $23.75 on the session purely because the metal rallied. Against a fixed assessed premium of $2,094 that leaves an implied market component of about $442.50, DOWN from $466.25 - so a 1.46% metal rally mechanically made the US premium look 5.1% less market-driven without one physical fact changing in the United States. THE COMPARISON THAT SIZES THE DISTORTION: US duty-paid at $2,094 is 4.3x European duty-unpaid at $485 and 5.3x the Japanese Q3 contract at $395 on the same metal at the same moment. Strip the $1,651.50 statutory wedge and the residual sits between the two.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC AND DATED: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT TODAY, 08-SEPTEMBER-2026, AND EXPLICITLY INCLUDE ALUMINIUM. Canada is applying 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on products drawn from those targeted by the US Section 338 and Section 232 measures, with each product's rate matched to the corresponding US rate; IN STEEL AND ALUMINIUM THE EXISTING 25% COUNTER-TARIFF RISES TO 50%. The package covers $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and is described by the Canadian government as matching the US Section 338 tariffs dollar for dollar after the US imposed 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL TARIFF HEADLINE: the Canada-United States corridor is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade route in the world, and it is now taxed in BOTH directions rather than one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A PHYSICAL READER IS DECOUPLING RATHER THAN SIMPLE INFLATION - regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border are mechanically supported because arbitrage between them is more expensive, while the volume that actually crosses is suppressed, so the delivered price and the exchange benchmark drift further apart. THE SECOND ACTIVE DRIVER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNRESOLVED: the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over any return of Persian Gulf supply, and Middle East LNG scarcity on tanker disruption continues to constrain regional refining and smelting.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.

flows.note: RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT TODAY AND EXPLICITLY INCLUDE ALUMINIUM. Counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium rise from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, within a package applying 15%, 25% and 50% rates across $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars. WATCH THE US MIDWEST AND CANADIAN DELIVERED PREMIUMS RATHER THAN THE EXCHANGE PRICE: the mechanical effect is to support regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border while suppressing cross-border volume.

EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECISION WITH A 25 BASIS POINT RISE FULLY PRICED. Euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. BECAUSE THE RISE IS FULLY PRICED THE MARKET-MOVING CONTENT IS THE GUIDANCE, and the risk is two-sided: dovish framing would be read as the end of the cycle, any signal of a follow-up extends the tightening path into 2027. The European leg matters disproportionately here because European restart economics are already marginal on energy cost and the duty-unpaid premium must absorb the Russian import ban at year end.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE DATE IN THE NEAR TERM. August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with June and July revised up a combined 55,000, unemployment steady at 4.1% and participation up to 61.6%, and traders moved to price the possibility of a HIKE. THE OPEN QUESTION HAS FLIPPED FROM WHETHER THE FED CUTS TO WHETHER IT RAISES. Direct headwind for a dollar-priced metal; simultaneously a brake on the restart pipeline through the discount rate, so the net effect on the physical balance is ambiguous even where the effect on price is not.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly on this cadence; the September anode settlement is already public at 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t acceptance, and coal tar pitch has not printed a newer mark since 13-August. SMM EXPECTS SEPTEMBER ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE BOTH TO RISE WHILE THE MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE DECLINES, so the cost stack is moving two ways at once and total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone.

WHETHER THE INVENTORY DRAW RESUMES OR THE STALL PERSISTS. Stock was unchanged at 244,525 tonnes on 07-September - a published change of exactly zero - and has drawn only 2,400 tonnes across the last fifteen sessions, under 0.1% per session. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SERIES ON THE PAGE RIGHT NOW because the bull case rests on an inventory level whose flow has stopped confirming it. Watch it alongside the cash-3M spread: a resumed draw with a widening backwardation would validate the tightness thesis; a continued stall with the spread pinned near flat would not.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-$325 per tonne against the Q3 record of $395, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. Talks began the week of 24-August and run through later this month. THE PENDING RANGE HERE IS HELD AT $290-325 AND HAS NOT BEEN NARROWED because no newer dated public report printed this run. The settlement is the single clearest public read on Asian physical tightness available.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it, and at a last assessment of $485/t - below its own trailing average, with the published rationale for lower Q4 Japanese offers explicitly citing SOFTER European premiums - it is not currently behaving as though the event is coming. Either replacement units are already sourced, or the event is not yet priced; the assessment cadence is too slow to tell which.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. RAISED TO A HIGHER CONVICTION THIS RUN ON A DATED, MATERIAL EVENT RATHER THAN ON DRIFT: NORTH AMERICAN TRADE FRAGMENTATION ESCALATED TODAY. Canada's counter-tariffs take effect on 08-September and explicitly include aluminium, with counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium rising from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE. That risk has now materially increased: the largest primary-aluminium trade corridor in the world is taxed in both directions, which mechanically supports delivered premiums on both sides of the border while suppressing the volume that actually crosses and decoupling regional prices from the exchange benchmark. THE US SECTION 232 RATE ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND VERIFIED AT 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE PIPELINE GAINED FURTHER PUBLIC CONFIRMATION. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. Slovalco is restarting the first 75,000 tonnes of 175,000 tonnes total under an agreement with the Slovak government on carbon cost compensation, guided to begin in Q4-2026. Alcoa's San Ciprian has restarted and is close to full capacity on energy hedging secured through 2027, and Alcoa completed the restart of 15,000 tonnes at Portland in Q2-2026. Century's Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015. EGA HAS 315 OF AL TAWEELAH'S 1,262 CELLS BACK ONLINE with the refinery near 50% and pre-war output reaffirmed for Q1-2027, and is separately in talks with the US government over incentives for a US smelter. THE COMMON FEATURE OF EVERY ENTRY IS THAT A POWER SOLUTION CAME FIRST, which is exactly why this week's hawkish rate repricing is a real brake on the pipeline even while the pipeline widens.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. RAISED TO UP. MACRO TIGHTENING RISK IS NOW THE CLEAREST NEAR-TERM PRICE HEADWIND AND TWO DATED DECISIONS LAND INSIDE EIGHT DAYS. The European Central Bank decides Thursday 10-September with a 25 basis point rise fully priced after euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. The US Federal Reserve follows Wednesday 16-September after August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with prior months revised up a combined 55,000 and participation rising to 61.6%; traders moved to price the possibility of a HIKE. THE REGIME HAS FLIPPED FROM 'WILL THEY CUT' TO 'WILL THEY RAISE' INSIDE A FORTNIGHT. For a dollar-priced industrial metal this is a direct headwind, and the second-order effect cuts the other way by raising the discount rate on every restart decision - which is why this risk is rated High impact but is not straightforwardly bearish for the physical balance.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE MIDDLE EAST DISRUPTION REMAINS THE ONE PILLAR OF THE BULL CASE THAT HAS NOT WEAKENED, AND IT ESCALATED AGAIN. Trading Economics commentary current at this compile states that the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over the potential return of aluminium supplies from the Persian Gulf, and that Middle East LNG supply, essential for refining, has been scarce on tanker disruption in the Strait. THE UNDERLYING CAPACITY LOSS IS OBSERVABLE IN PUBLIC COMPANY DISCLOSURE RATHER THAN INFERRED: Qatalum is at roughly 60% of its 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a second Hydro force majeure on aluminium sales outstanding, and Aluminium Bahrain has had reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026, 19% of 1,623,000 tonnes, with no restart announced. NEITHER HAS A PUBLISHED RESOLUTION DATE, which is what distinguishes them from the scheduled restart pipeline and is why they still carry the bull case.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND THE TRIGGER WORD IS STILL 'TEMPORARY'. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN. Alunorte, the world's largest alumina refinery outside China, has ramped back to full capacity from its August cut to 50% ON A TEMPORARY TERMINAL-ACCESS AGREEMENT WITH ITS GAS SUPPLIER. The restoration relieves cost today and removes a cost-push support from the metal price; the temporariness is the exposure. SMM SEPARATELY EXPECTS THE SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE on surplus, high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup, WHILE PREBAKED ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE BOTH RISE. THE COST STACK IS THEREFORE MOVING IN TWO DIRECTIONS AT ONCE and the direction of total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone. Bauxite remains the least-watched and most geographically concentrated link, with roughly two tonnes of alumina required per tonne of metal, so a bauxite disruption propagates with a lag.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. CHINESE EXPORT SUPPLY IS THE PRINCIPAL MECHANISM RELIEVING THE WESTERN SHORTAGE AND THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED BEARISH FACT ON THIS PAGE. Exports rose 18.7% year on year in July, with public commentary attributing the surge to muted domestic demand allowing producers to ship out despite Beijing's 45-million-tonne output cap. THE MECHANISM MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER: the relieving metal arrives as semi-finished and alloy product that does not pass through LME warehouses, which is one coherent explanation for how a thirty-six-year exchange inventory low can coexist with a front-month curve that will not pay more than two dollars for prompt metal. The output ceiling and the export flow are both real and are not contradictory.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. MOVED FROM FLAT TO UP, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE RE-RATING THIS RUN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. Exchange stock was UNCHANGED at 244,525 tonnes on 07-September - a published change of exactly ZERO - and has fallen just 2,400 tonnes across the fifteen sessions from 17-August to 07-September, under 0.1% of the total per session. LEVEL AND FLOW HAVE SEPARATED: the thirty-six-year low is real and remains the strongest single support for the price, but the draw that produced it has flattened to a stop. A market being drained does not look like this. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS REPORTED FOR BALANCE: Shanghai inventories fell 3% week on week, so the two visible series now disagree. Until the London flow resumes, the inventory statistic should be treated as a floor under the price rather than as a trigger for the next leg higher.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE CURVE SIGNAL IS TOO SMALL TO ACT ON IN EITHER DIRECTION. Cash settled $2.00 ABOVE three-month on 07-September, a BACKWARDATION and the second such print in five sessions, against $0.50 contango on both 03- and 04-September, $2.00 backwardation on 02-September and $19.00 contango on 28-August. THE FRONT OF THE CURVE HAS NOW BEEN WITHIN $2.00 OF FLAT FOR SIX CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS. Two-hundredths of one percent is directionally meaningful and economically trivial, and the August average spread was a $1.60 CONTANGO, so the current print is barely outside the recent mean. THE CROSS-METAL COMPARISON IS THE USEFUL DIAGNOSTIC AND IT IS UNFLATTERING: on the same board zinc carries a $182.00 backwardation and copper $92.00, both WIDENING against rising visible stock. That is what a curve paying for prompt metal looks like, and aluminium - with the tightest inventory of the group relative to its own history - is not doing it.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT 31-DECEMBER-2026 AND IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS A DISORDERLY EUROPEAN SUPPLY RESET. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it and it is NOT BEHAVING AS IF THE EVENT IS COMING: duty-unpaid was last assessed at $485/t, below its own trailing average, and the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese producer offers explicitly cites SOFTER premiums in Europe. TWO READINGS ARE LIVE AND THE ASSESSMENT CADENCE IS TOO SLOW TO DISTINGUISH THEM: either the market has already sourced replacement units and the ban is priced, or the event is not yet in the price at all. The second reading is the risk, and it becomes harder to hedge the closer the date comes.

RE-ASSESSED 08-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED TO DOWN - THE ONLY RISK IMPROVING THIS RUN, AND IT IMPROVED ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE PASSAGE OF TIME. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SOURCE-DATA INTEGRITY: that the public price source this page depends on fails to publish, publishes stale cached snapshots, or disagrees with itself. THE TWO-RUN PUBLICATION GAP IS CLOSED. Both the 04-September and 07-September officials are public, and the 04-September aluminium settlement of $3,292.50 landed FIFTEEN CENTS from the independent CFD reference this page carried in commentary while refusing to write any figure into the official board. THE CONTROL WORKED EXACTLY AS DESIGNED: the board was held, the hold was disclosed on every dependent panel, nothing was invented, and nothing needed unwinding when the truth arrived. RESIDUAL EXPOSURE REMAINS AND IS WHY THIS IS NOT RATED LOWER: the per-metal aluminium and copper daily tables still end at 04-September while the two overviews and the nickel, zinc and lead tables carry 07-September, so the source is still internally uneven and those two rows required arithmetic reconciliation to the tonne before use.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

THE TWO-RUN PUBLICATION GAP IS CLOSED AND THE HOLD WAS VINDICATED.
